before.html:
Question 1
?

Find the slope of y=f(x) at x=3 if f(x)=11cos⁡x−sec⁡x+1x.

a
−sin⁡(3)−csc⁡(3)cot⁡(3)−13
b
−11sin⁡(3)−sec⁡(3)tan⁡(3)−13
c
11sin⁡(3)−sec⁡(3)tan⁡(3)−13
d
−11sin⁡(3)−csc⁡(3)cot⁡(3)−1
e
−11sin⁡(3)+sec⁡(3)tan⁡(3)+13
Submit

decision.explanation: The slope is f'(√3). Differentiating gives f'(x)=-11sin(x)-sec(x)tan(x)-1/x². Substituting x=√3 gives option b, since (√3)²=3.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Find the slope of $y=f(x)$ at $x=\sqrt{3}$ if $f(x)=11\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\frac{1}{x}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative using the sum rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(11\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(11\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x+{x}^{-1}) \\  & =11(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}} \\  & =-11\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=\sqrt{3}$ in the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\sqrt{3}) & =-11\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\operatorname{sec}⁡(\sqrt{3})\operatorname{tan}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\frac{1}{(\sqrt{3})^{2}} \\  & =-11\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\operatorname{sec}⁡(\sqrt{3})\operatorname{tan}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the slope of y=f(x) at x=3 if f(x)=11cos⁡x−sec⁡x+1x.

a

b

c

−11sin⁡(3)−csc⁡(3)cot⁡(3)−1
e

Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we calculate the derivative using the sum rule:

f′(x)=ddx(11cos⁡x−sec⁡x+1x)=ddx(11cos⁡x−sec⁡x+x−1)=11(−sin⁡x)−sec⁡xtan⁡x−1x2=−11sin⁡x−sec⁡xtan⁡x−1x2

Then, we substitute x=3 in the derivative and get f′(3)=−11sin⁡(3)−sec⁡(3)tan⁡(3)−1(3)2=−11sin⁡(3)−sec⁡(3)tan⁡(3)−13.

content.problem: Find the slope of $y=f(x)$ at $x=\sqrt{3}$ if $f(x)=11\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\frac{1}{x}.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative using the sum rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(11\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(11\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x+{x}^{-1}) \\  & =11(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}} \\  & =-11\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=\sqrt{3}$ in the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\sqrt{3}) & =-11\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\operatorname{sec}⁡(\sqrt{3})\operatorname{tan}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\frac{1}{(\sqrt{3})^{2}} \\  & =-11\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\operatorname{sec}⁡(\sqrt{3})\operatorname{tan}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
